title: Juventus 4-1 Omonia Nicosia: Conceicao stars to avert shock European defeat
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutJuventus 4-1 Omonia Nicosia: Conceicao stars to avert shock European defeatShareJuventus kept within touching distance of Bournemouth at the top of the Europa League standings with a routine win over Omonia Nicosia.Francisco Conceicao starred for Juventus as they came from behind to defeat Omonia Nicosia 4-1 in the Europa League.

Lubomir Satka headed Omonia into an early lead at Allianz Stadium, but Conceicao assisted Andrea Cambiaso and Jeff Ekhator before scoring himself, while Jeremie Boga rounded off the victory for the Bianconeri.

Conceicao saw an early effort parried away by Thomas Kaminski as Juve started on the front foot, but Omonia scored against the run of play in the 15th minute as Satka headed in from Muamer Tankovic's corner.
Kaminski was alert again to keep out a driven strike from Juan Cabal, though the Belgian could do nothing to keep out Cambiaso's curler into the top-left corner from distance in the 37th minute.

Ekhator then scored his first goal for the Bianconeri, firing through the legs of Kaminski after being played through by Conceicao, while Federico Gatti saw a first-time effort blocked by the foot of Kaminski before the break.

Juve maintained their momentum and saw Ekhator flash over the bar from close range, but Conceicao doubled their lead in the 68th minute, scoring on the rebound after his initial shot from close range was saved.

Boga ensured all three points five minutes later, cutting in from the left wing and curling into the top-right corner to see Juve move up to second in the league-phase table, two points behind Bournemouth.

Ahead of this encounter, Spalletti revealed Ekhator would get minutes in order to give Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani some rest, and the youngster did exactly what his head coach would have hoped for.

On his first competitive start for the club, Ekhator (20 years and 15 days) became the youngest Italian player to score for Juve in a major European competition since Niccolo Giannetti (19 years and 218 days) against Manchester City in December 2010, also in the Europa League.
However, it was Conceicao's performance which helped Juve avoid a potential scare, with the winger featuring for the first time since October 18 after being sidelined with a shoulder injury.
Conceicao led the match in shots (seven), touches in the box (nine), chances created (four), passes in the final third (26), successful dribbles (5/8) and duels won (7/11).

Aside from the goal they conceded, Spalletti will be delighted with his side's display as they won the expected goals (xG) battle 2.07 to 0.77, while he was also able to rest key players ahead of a tough test against Como at the weekend.
